_comment: Template study config. Copy this file, rename it, and fill in your own corpus — pass it via --config. Required: corpora, and study (the roles the scripts you run use — see README step 4). languages is needed for stopwords and spaCy/Stanza models. output, chunking, embedding_model (default sentence-transformers/LaBSE), analysis, lexical_richness and the other tuning sections are optional with defaults. Everything after '_optional_sections_comment' is only read by the script named in its _comment; delete sections for scripts you won't run (each script checks for the ones it needs). Language codes are your own choice (see README's Config section, 'Language codes') — this template uses 'en'/'fr' as illustrative placeholders only, not a requirement. Any key starting with '_' is treated as a comment and skipped everywhere the toolkit iterates a section, so you can annotate your own config the same way.

output._comment: Written under the working directory unless you set 'root' or pass --output-root (--output-root wins over 'root'). Absolute paths are used as-is.

en._comment: spacy_model (+ optional spacy_model_fallback) is needed if this language is used with adjective_window.py or dependency_parsing.py, or as primary_language for cross_corpus_dependency.py. stanza_model is needed if this is your comparison_language. stopwords_file, keep_short_tokens, and adjective_suffixes are all optional tokenizer tuning — see README. stopwords_file is looked for next to this config file, under the working directory, then among the lists bundled with the package. Set it to "spacy" to use spaCy's built-in list for this language code, or "spacy:<lang>" (e.g. "spacy:it") when your code is not spaCy's (needs the parsing extra, no model).

fr._comment: For cross_corpus_frequency.py, configure a stopwords_file for BOTH languages or for neither — removing stopwords from only one side biases the per-10k rates and Dunning scores.

author_a_work._comment: type is 'single_file' (one continuous text) or 'collection' (a directory of dated/grouped items, see author_a_collection below). path is relative to corpus_root / --corpus-root.
author_a_work.label: Author A's Work
author_a_work.author: author_a

author_a_collection._comment: For type 'collection': path is a directory containing one subdirectory per entry in 'groups', each holding .txt files (one file per dated/grouped item). Omit 'groups' if the .txt files sit directly in path. Group names label the plots and CSVs.
author_a_collection.label: Author A's Collection
author_a_collection.author: author_a

author_b_work._comment: strip_after_marker is optional: drop everything from a marker line onward, e.g. an editorial apparatus section.
author_b_work.label: Author B's Work
author_b_work.author: author_b

chunking._comment: Chunks for embedding: paragraphs merged up to max_chars characters (longer paragraphs are split at sentences, then lines, then whitespace); min_chars only drops a whole text shorter than it (0 keeps everything); chunks of a longer text, the last included, can be shorter when a paragraph break and max_chars force a flush. Collection items shorter than collection_item_min_chars are skipped; items at or below collection_item_split_threshold are kept whole (so they can be longer than max_chars); longer items are chunked as above but with collection_item_min_chars in place of min_chars. Encoders truncate long input: LaBSE reads 256 word-pieces and silently ignores the rest, and medieval Italian and Latin run about 3.9 characters per word-piece, so 800 characters fills the window and 1600 loses the second half of most chunks. xlt-embed-corpus warns when chunks exceed the model's window and suggests a max_chars for your corpus.

_optional_sections_comment: Everything below is optional. Each section is read by exactly one script — delete a section if you won't run that script.

analysis._comment: Used by analysis_a_umap.py. n_permutations shuffles for the permutation test (p is never below 1/(n_permutations+1)).

lexical_richness._comment: Used by lexical_richness.py. mattr_window is in tokens; lower it for short texts, or the whole work collapses to a single TTR value. smoothing_window is in per-window TTR values. Both must be positive integers.

term_frequency_clusters._comment: Used by term_frequency.py. One entry per concept cluster; 'terms' are surface forms in primary_language to count together (a list, matched case-insensitively). Clusters are counted independently, so a word may count toward several.

adjective_window._comment: Used by adjective_window.py. window is the number of tokens on each side of an anchor term.

adjective_anchor_terms._comment: Used by adjective_window.py. Each key is an anchor concept; its list is that concept's surface forms in primary_language.

dependency_parsing._comment: Used by dependency_parsing.py. chunk_chars is how much text is fed to spaCy at once.

dependency_agents._comment: Used by dependency_parsing.py. role is a dependency label (e.g. 'nsubj', 'obj'); passive and English-convention spellings (nsubjpass, nsubj:pass, dobj) are matched automatically.

cross_corpus_concept_clusters._comment: Used by cross_corpus_frequency.py. Each cluster has one key per language code (must match your languages' codes) holding that language's surface/inflected forms for the same concept (both languages are required). A token counts toward the first cluster that lists it only.

cross_corpus_dependency._comment: Used by cross_corpus_dependency.py. agent_a/agent_b are arbitrary role names — see README. 'primary' is spaCy-side (lemmas, primary_language); 'comparison' is Stanza-side (surface forms, comparison_language), and needs languages[comparison_language].stanza_model.

stylometry._comment: Used by stylometry.py (xlt-stylometry): same-language stylometry (Burrows's / Cosine Delta, General Imposters). Every corpus it reads must share one language. Only 'groups' is required. A selector is a corpus id (the whole corpus), '<corpus_id>:<group>' (one configured group of a collection) or '<corpus_id>:<group>/<item>' (one item: its file name without .txt). groups_file is an optional CSV (header: group,selector) whose rows add to groups; it is looked for next to this config file, then under the working directory. corpora (optional; default: no restriction) restricts which corpora selectors and rolling.corpus may use. Stopword lists are NOT applied: function words are the signal. mfw: number of most frequent words used as features (200). sample_words: tokens per sample (2000; Delta is unreliable below a few thousand words per sample). strip_patterns: regular expressions (multiline) removed before tokenizing, e.g. fixed opening and closing formulas. exclude_words: never features, e.g. proper names. distance: 'cosine_delta' (default) or 'burrows_delta'. imposters: groups forming the General Imposters pool; verification: questioned/candidate pairs, neither in imposters. iterations (100) and feature_fraction (0.5) tune General Imposters; random_seed (42) fixes every random choice. rolling (optional): windows of window_words tokens (2000) every step_words (500) across one corpus, each scored against the reference groups. A text in two groups, or twice in one, is a warning, not an error.

groups._comment: Group names are your own; these are placeholders.

parallel_passages._comment: Used by parallel_passages.py (xlt-parallel-passages): find where the source corpus translates, quotes or paraphrases the target corpora, sentence by sentence, with the embedding_model. Reads the raw texts (xlt-embed-corpus need not have run); sentence embeddings are cached as embeddings/parallel_<corpus_id>_sentences.npy. Only source and targets are required. source: the corpus id whose sentences are searched for. targets: non-empty list of corpus ids to search in, not including source. min_sentence_chars (40): shorter sentences are skipped. max_sentence_chars (600): longer sentences are wrapped into pieces of at most this length (below min_sentence_chars is accepted with a warning). sentence_split: regular expression that splits each paragraph into sentences (default: after . ? ! ; : followed by whitespace, and after the CJK 。！？ with or without whitespace). location_patterns (optional): {corpus_id: regex}; a sentence's location is the last match (group 1 if the regex has a group) in its text up to and including it, e.g. chapter headings, matched with re.MULTILINE; otherwise the collection item (group/item) or p<paragraph number> of a single file. threshold (0.70): minimum cosine similarity for a match. Matches are merged into runs separately for each target text (collection item or single file): a passage is a run of matches into one target text in source order with at most merge_gap (5) source sentences between consecutive matches, whatever those sentences matched (a match into another text does not end the run, so passages into different texts may overlap), the target index moving forward by at most target_window (10) sentences or back by 1; it needs at least min_passage_sentences (2) matches. align (true): align each passage's source span with its target span extended by align_context (2) target sentences each side, in groups of 1-3 sentences per side; skip_penalty (0.35) is the cost of leaving a sentence unaligned.

topic_modeling._comment: Used by analysis_b_topics.py. min_topic_size is the smallest number of chunks BERTopic will call a topic — lower it for small corpora (minimum 2). The remaining keys are language codes; extra_stopwords supplements load_stopwords(), keep_stopwords exempts specific words from removal.
